OPTION AXIS -- THE ONE REAL INFERENCE, AND IT CONTRADICTS THE PAPER. The S2 questionnaire lists every item's options in the order 'Definitely agree / Agree / Neither / Disagree / Definitely disagree', while the article's Methods states the items were 'rated on a 5-point Likert scale, ranging from 1 point (strongly disagree) to 5 points (strongly agree)'. The two cannot both describe the deposited S1 codes. Shipped anchors follow the questionnaire's display order (1=Definitely agree .. 5=Definitely disagree) on three grounds: (a) the same file's demographic codes follow that display order and reconcile exactly with the paper's own numbers -- gender 1=172/2=137 vs Table 2 Male 172 / Female 137; education codes 3+4 = 90.3% vs the text's '90.3% had a bachelor's degree or above'; age codes 1+2 = 88.3% vs 'Most (88.5%) were aged between 20-40'; (b) under the Methods reading the average respondent disagrees with all 40 items of the questionnaire, including mutually opposing content (every item mean is 1.92-2.71), whereas the display-order reading makes it ordinary acquiescence; (c) marker items in the same instrument: 'I will switch to an NEV if they are safer and more reliable' (1.92) and '...smarter and technology-intensive' (1.96) are the two most extreme items in the whole survey, which is only sensible as strongest AGREEMENT, and 'I am driving and will continue to drive an NEV' (2.71) is the least endorsed BI item, as expected of a sample the paper describes as potential rather than current users.
